summary: feat(sync): delete mirror rows a complete, unwindowed pull no longer serves (issue #17)
reason: No sync path ever DELETEd a mirror row. The only DELETE from `resources` was the hand-authored ClearCompanyResources, reachable solely through `sync --full --company S --resources R`, and upsertGenericResourceTx overwrites the blob and restamps synced_at/updated_at on every write, so a re-fetched row and a row nobody re-fetched are indistinguishable. A record deleted in Fiken stayed in the mirror forever and every detector and the MCP sql tool kept reporting it (issue #17). Fiken has no negative-delta channel to use instead: sales, purchases and transactions are soft-deleted (payload `deleted: true` plus a reverse transaction, which a re-pull picks up anyway), contacts answer 204 or `inactive: true`, and products, projects, inbox documents, drafts, time entries and contact persons are HARD deletes with no flag and no listing of what went. The only evidence is an absence. THE RULE is therefore a set difference per (company, resource), taken at the end of that company's walk: mirror rows minus the distinct storage keys the walk landed (landedIDs, which issue #15 already builds and resets per parent). An absence is only evidence when the walk saw the WHOLE collection, so syncPruneDeletedRows (internal/cli/sync_deletes.go) acts only when the pull was not windowed (syncPullWindow.AllowsDeletion - a --since or --param pull asked for a subset and every unchanged row is absent by construction), the walk was not truncated (no --max-pages cap, no resumed or stuck cursor, no non-JSON body, no transport or upsert error), Fiken-Api-Result-Count was present, and the distinct rows landed EQUAL that count. That last condition is issue #15's completeness check and it is what makes the sweep safe against issue #12's failure class: a walk that silently skipped a page would otherwise read the whole page as deletions. A 403 parent is covered by the header condition - it serves no page and no header, so its empty landed set can never read as 'this collection is empty'. When only the count condition fails, the run emits sync_warning reason=deletes_skipped_count_mismatch beside the result_count_mismatch anomaly, because 'nothing was deleted, the mirror is clean' and 'nothing was deleted, the pull could not be trusted' must not look alike on the event stream. A successful sweep emits {"event":"sync_deleted","resource":..,"company":..,"count":n} only when n > 0 (a stream full of count:0 trains a reader to ignore the one that matters); --human-friendly gets a stderr line. THE GENERATED DIFF is one call, syncPruneDeletedRows(...), placed in syncDependentResource right after the per-parent result-count comparison, where parentPageInfo, parentTruncated, depLanded and depWindowedPull are all in scope and depLanded has not yet been reset for the next parent. Everything else is hand-authored. THE FLAT WALKER IS DELIBERATELY OUT: its only resource is `companies` itself, whose rows carry a bare storage key with no company scope in it (exactly the shape the store method refuses), and dropping a company row on the strength of one pull would orphan every dependent row of that company in the mirror - a far larger blast radius than this issue asks for, for an event (a company vanishing from Fiken) that is rare and visible. THE STORE HALF is store.DeleteCompanyResourcesNotIn(resourceType, slug, keep) in internal/store/mirror_deletes.go: one transaction, addressed exactly like ClearCompanyResources (resource_type plus json_extract(data, '$.parent_id')), same explicit-rowid resources_fts delete because modernc's FTS5 ignores DELETE WHERE column = ? on a virtual table. Two deliberate differences from ClearCompanyResources: a row whose id carries no `id\0<slug>` suffix is a pre-canonicalisation legacy row that another company's sync may have written, so an absence cannot be attributed to this company and the row is left alone (the --full --company repair clears those on purpose; a sweep must not); and the typed-table row is deleted too where the resource has one, since typed tables are keyed by the same storage id, UpsertBatch writes both in one transaction and `doctor` cross-checks the two counts - dropping only the generic row would trade a stale mirror for one that disagrees with itself and the MCP sql tool would keep serving the deleted record. (ClearCompanyResources not doing that is a pre-existing gap in the --full --company path, filed separately rather than copied here.) The difference is computed in Go over a streamed scan of the company's own ids rather than as a SQL NOT IN: journal_entries holds ~38k rows for one company, far past SQLite's variable limit, and a chunked NOT IN would delete every row merely absent from the chunk it was compared against; the statement count stays proportional to the rows that actually go, usually zero. An empty keep set is meaningful (the API said the collection is empty and the caller verified it against the header) but an empty slug is an error, so this can never widen into an unscoped wipe. NO TOMBSTONE and no deleted_at column (YAGNI, per the plan): the row goes, and Fiken's own soft `deleted` flags in sale, purchase and transaction payloads keep meaning what they meant. `--full --company` and the sweep do not fight: clearFullSyncCompanyRows runs before the walk, so by the time the sweep looks the mirror holds exactly what just landed and the difference is empty.

Hand-authored tests, all checked red against the pre-fix code: internal/cli/sync_deletes_test.go on the rowServer / deniedParentServer harnesses - CompletePullDeletesRowsTheAPIStoppedServing (3 rows land, the API then serves 2, the third is gone and one sync_deleted with count 1 says so, no anomaly), ShortPullDeletesNothingAndSaysSo (claims 3 serves 2: all 3 rows survive, one result_count_mismatch and one deletes_skipped_count_mismatch carrying result_count 3 / rows 2), WindowedPullDeletesNothing (--since returns 1 of 3 with a matching filtered header, so only AllowsDeletion stands between it and two deleted live rows), CappedRunDeletesNothing (--max-pages 1 with agreeing counts, so only the truncation flag can hold the sweep back), DeniedCompanyKeepsItsRows (two companies, one 403: its 3 rows are untouched while the other is swept, one sync_deleted naming good-co), BareLegacyRowsSurviveTheSweep (a bare-key row with parent_id in the blob survives a complete pull that did not serve it). internal/store/mirror_deletes_test.go - DeletesOnlyTheAbsentRowsOfThatCompany (also asserts the FTS index and the typed contacts table lost the row, with a positive search first so the negative is not vacuous), EmptyKeepSetClearsTheCompany, LeavesBareLegacyRowsAlone, KeepSetLargerThanTheSQLVariableLimit (2 800 rows, 2 500 kept, 300 deleted, well past SQLite's 999-variable default, plus an idempotent second sweep), RefusesUnscopableCalls (empty slug, a non-parent-keyed resource, an unknown resource name). The windowed, capped and legacy tests were each re-checked red with their guard removed. No live API call was made, no fiken write command was run, and no sync ran against a real company.
